page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-128 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by AMD EPYC 9J14 processors on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor.

Hardware acceleration and integrated disk resources are omitted from this configuration; the instance provides 0 GPUs and lists no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for operating systems and persistent data. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside dedicated processor core allocations that prevent multi-tenant CPU contention.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-efficient resource layout for compute-bound tasks where large physical thread counts are necessary but extreme memory footprints are unneeded. Common workloads matching this profile include distributed software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch media processing, computational modeling, and horizontally scaled web application layers.

It includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying on remote volumes for block persistence, and supplies one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource layout is suited to parallel compute tasks that benefit from high dedicated core counts without requiring large memory capacity per thread. Workloads well aligned with this profile include distributed continuous integration builds, batch processing pipelines, simulation workloads, and high-throughput application backends.
